newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire now ruled by military dictatorship - Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Zaire now ruled by military dictatorship - Belgium.

text.p: Zaire is currently in the hands of a military dictatorship which has suspended moves towards democratisation in the central African country, Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said on Thursday.
It is "a military dictatorship revisited, with a military man as prime minister and the parliament thrown aside," he told a news conference on recent developments in war-torn Zaire.

Derycke likened the current political situation in Zaire to events in 1965 before President Mobutu Sese Seko came to power, but declined to condemn outright Mobutu's appointment of General Likulia Bolongo as prime minister on Wednesday.

He reiterated that "politically the page of Mobutu was turned over some time ago, but Mobutu is still there with the DSP and FAZ (forming) a clique around the president...I said a long time ago post-Mobutism is here."
The DSP is Mobutu's presidential guard, made up of elite and well-paid troops. The FAZ is Zaire's regular army, which has a reputation for being disorganised, undisciplined and badly paid.

Derycke said talks between Belgium and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces control about a third of the country after months of fighting, did not constitute a formal recognition of Mobutu's opponent.
